chapter: On the road with Duke and his bandmates
title: Questions about being the white man in Duke's band
summary: He recounts a Dallas man asking why he played with Black musicians, and says no one ever really objected.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Was there ever any question down south about your being with the band and your not being black?

Oh, one place -- let me see if I can remember -- I think it was in Canada or someplace, but they asked me about what I was -- they said, 'What are you doing playing with' ... oh, no; that was in Dallas, Texas. In Dallas, Texas, we were getting ready to play, and there were a lot of people there, and people started looking at me, especially this fellow on the right side of the bandstand, and I thought to myself, 'I know he's going to be asking me some questions soon.' He said, 'You don't mind giving me an autograph?' and I said, 'You don't want no autograph; I know what you want -- you want to ask me a question about me.' He said, 'What are

you doing playing with these niggers?" I said, "Let me tell you something; you see that man over there on the piano? You know he is a Negro, but he got more respect than a lot of white people put together, you know? He got more recognition yet, too, because (unintelligible) you couldn't come to a dance dressed in overalls and so forth, you know. So I didn't give him no autograph or nothing.
Did anybody ever object in the south?

No, just like I said, they would say, "What you doing playing with a bunch of niggers when you can play with a bunch of white men?" -- and I would say, "I don't want to -- I like it with this band more than anything else. This is a famous band. I like it with everybody."

You didn't ever run in to any place that had a law, because once Willie Smith told me once that when Harry's band, they ran into someplace that had a law that said you couldn't have black and white on the same bandstand, and there a group Rubba was waiting for him, and so Harry said, "Okay, show me the one who isn't white" -- and nobody could tell that Willie wasn't white, he was so light.
Oh, he closed the stage door when we were on the bandstand; he should have told the man not to let anybody in there.
But there was never any difficulty with Duke's band like that? in the South? Except some questions once in a while.
No, no. I don't think so. Just
